JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 164/163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Shaik Ismail Jabeeulla who met with road traffic accident.

2. That on 14-01-2022 at about 5-30 p.m., the deceased was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP -39- AR-2147 along with pillion rider one Sri Siddiq very slowly carefully and cautiously on the correct side of the road in order go their village near Thirupathi and when they reached near Kothavaripalle cross, Madanapalle Mandal, at that time all of a sudden the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-CQ-4227 came from cross road to enter the NH road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased , result of which the deceased and the pillion rider of the motorcycle fell down and sustained injuries and both of them succumbed to the injuries.
2(a). Deceased Shaik Ismail Jabeeulla was aged about 25 years, he was a coolie and earning Rs.40,000/- per annum.
Due to the sudden death of deceased, petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03- CQ-4227 has remained absent he was placed ex-parte.

4. The respondent no 2 though appeared through counsel but as the vehicle in question had no insurance policy as per the order of this court dated 03-09-2024 the respondent no 2 was deleted from the proceedings.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following points are framed:
POINTS

1 . Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Shaik Imam Hussain died on account of road traffic accident on 14-01-2022 at about 5-30 p.m, at Kothavaripalle corss,
Mandanapalle Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh State, due to involvement of motorcycle bearing No.AP- 39-AR-2147 and motorcycle bearing Reg. no.AP-03-CQ-4227?

The petitioner No.1 got examined himself as Pw1 and Ex.P1 to Ex.P.10 is tendered during the evidence on petitioners' side.

The respondent no.1 has not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and learned counsel for respondent no.1.
8.

My findings on the above points are as follows:-
 Points No.1 : In the Affirmative  Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Point No.3 : As per final order,
 for the following;
 REASONS 9.
Point No.1: The petitioners are the parents of the deceased .

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, charge sheet, spot mahazar, spot sketchs,
IMV report, Inquest.

10. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Tekumavi Reddeppa, case has been registered against the rider/deceased who is the rider of motorcycle bearing No.AP-39-AR-2147 in Crime No.15/2022 of Chittoor Police Station for the offence punishable under section 304-A IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of motorcycle bearing No.AP-39-AR-2147 for the offences punishable under Section 304-A of IPC.
11.

It is not in dispute that petitioners have filed this petition u/Sec.164 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988.
If claim petition is filed u/Sec.164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the petitioners need not prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
It is sufficient if they prove the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the vehicle resulting in injuries and death of the deceased.
12. In support of their case the petitioners have got examined the first petitioner as PW.1 who has reiterated the petition averments.
13. As observed supra in a petition under section 163(A) of IMV Act, the aspect of negligence has no role whatsoever to play to decide the question of entitlement for compensation.

14. In the petition filed under section 163-A, the question to be considered by the tribunal is the involvement of vehicle against which the compensation is sought for and not whether there is rash Shaik Imam Hussain vs Aruna T on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128536723/
3 or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed.
The aspect of negligence has no role whatsoever to decide the question of entitlement for compensation. Section 163- A of the act itself lays down that:
"not withstanding anything contained in this act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in case of death or permanent disablement due to the accident arising out of use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the second schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim as the case may be"
15.

sentences.text: In a ruling relied by the learned counsel for petitioner reported in 2018 ACJ 1 SC between United Indian Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Sunil Kumar & Anr.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Sunil Kumar & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The question was raised whether in claim proceedings u/Sec. 163-A is it open to the Insurance Company to raise the defence/plea of negligence of victim.

It was held that "permitting Insurance Company to raise defence of negligence would bring proceedings u/Sec. 163-A at par with proceedings u/Sec. 166 which would not only be self contradictory but also defeats the very legislative intention".

16. In view of the above provision of law and case law, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 163-A of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered is whether vehicle against which the claim is made is involved in the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P6 this court is of the opinion that the accident was occurred due to involvement or use of the offending vehicle and motorcycle in the accident and in that the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries Accordingly, point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
17. Issue no 3 : Admittedly this petition is filed u/Sec.163 -A of IMV Act.

As per the notification dated 25-05-2018 issued by the Central Government, the following amendment was made to the Second Schedule of the MV Act:
"THE SECOND SCHEDULE SCHEDULE FOR COMPENSATION FOR THIRD PARTY FATAL ACCIDENTS/INURY CASES CLAIMS 1. (a) Fatal Accidents:
Compensation payable in case of Death shall be five lakh rupees.

(b) Accidents resulting in permanent disability: Compensation payable shall be =Rs.5,00,000/- x percentage disability as per Schedule I of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923)} : Provided that the minimum compensation in case of permanent disability of any kind shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees.
(c) Accidents resulting in minor injury: A fixed compensation of twenty five thousand rupees shall be payable:

sentences.text: On and from the date of 1st day of January, 2019 the amount of compensation specified in the clauses (a) and (c) of paragraph (1) shall stand increased by 5 per cent annually".
3. This notification shall come into form on the date of its publication in the official Gazette".
18. According to the above notification, compensation payable in case of death shall be five lakh rupees.
Further to keep up with the cost of living in future, the compensation amount will increase by five percent annually in these type of cases with effect from 1st January 2019.
The said proviso would apply only to the cases comes under clause (a) and (c) but not (b).
19. Hence in view of the Gazetted notification referred above the petitioners are entitled for fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

The calculation table stands as follows:
Total compensation : Rs.5,00,000-00 awarded 20.
As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.2, the offending vehicle was not having insurance policy as on the date of accident.

Hence, the owner of the offending vehicle ie., respondent no.1 is directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners along with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Point No.2 is answered.
21. Point No.3:-
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
ORDER The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total com- pensation of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakh only ).
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award Out of the compensation amount,
Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/-, Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.3,00,000/-

Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 2 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners No.1 and 2 on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
